title: Embedding quantization profiles (INT8/FP16) and cosine-similarity drift checks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce validated INT8 and FP16 quantization profiles for our embedding models and put in place automated cosine-similarity drift checks to ensure semantic search quality stays within SLA during rollouts and in production. Scope includes: building a reproducible calibration workflow, generating per-layer and per-channel scale tables for INT8, producing FP16 variants for hardware fallback, defining acceptance thresholds using cosine similarity and downstream recall@k tests, and adding a monitoring job that triggers alerts when embedding drift exceeds thresholds. This ticket focuses on the engineering work: calibration harness, batch quantizer integration in the model conversion pipeline, evaluation harness that computes per-query cosine statistics vs FP32 baseline, and a canary rollout recipe for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can produce reproducible INT8 scale tables for embedding models with a fixed seed and documented dataset split
FP16 model variant exported and verified for parity on numerical stable ops (no catastrophic NaNs)
End-to-end validation report comparing quantized vs FP32 baseline: mean cosine similarity >= 0.995 and 99th percentile cosine drop <= 0.02 across the canonical eval set
Automated drift check job in Console that computes daily cohort cosine distributions and raises an alert if mean drops > 0.01 or recall@10 drops > 1.5%
Canary rollout procedure documented: 5% traffic for 48h with auto-rollback on drift alerts
Integration tests added to CI to ensure quantized artifacts load and produce deterministic embeddings for a fixed input seed
calibration_workflow: 1) Dataset selection: use embedding-calib-v2 (10k samples stratified across customers & lengths). Store a reproducible sample in s3://redwood-emb-calib/ENG-4973/
2) Preprocess: normalize tokens/inputs with same tokenizer version used in production, record token lengths distribution for kernel selection heuristics
3) Warm-up run: collect activation ranges and per-channel statistics with FP32 forward pass (MV statistics), use 16-bit accumulators for stability
4) Compute scales: evaluate symmetric and asymmetric schemes, produce per-tensor and per-channel scale tables, store as JSON profiles attached to model artifact
5) Quantize weights/activations: generate INT8 artifacts using chosen kernels; also export FP16 variant with same graph changes
6) Sanity checks: verify no out-of-range activations, run small-batch inference and check outputs shape/consistency
7) Publish artifacts: attach quantization_profile.json and calibration_seed metadata to the model bundle in model-registry
validation_plan: Baseline: generate FP32 embeddings for eval set (50k queries + 100k corpus) and compute reference cosine similarity and recall@k
Quantized eval: run INT8 and FP16 variants on identical inputs, compute per-query cosine, delta statistics, and aggregate metrics (mean, std, p50/p95/p99, recall@1/5/10)
Drift metric thresholds: mean cosine >= 0.995, p1 cosine >= 0.92, 99th percentile cosine drop <= 0.02, recall@10 drop <= 1.5%
Failure modes to capture: systematically lower similarity for long-string inputs, quantization bias for low-norm vectors, edge-case tokens producing NaNs
Tooling: publish a human-readable validation report (HTML) and machine-readable JSON summary to S3, and attach to PR in GitHub
Sign-off: PM + RESEARCH review the report and add approval in the ticket comments before canary rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal CI validation and perf profiling on a small Dedicated pool
Stage 2: Canary - 5% of production traffic routed to quantized model for 48 hours; monitor cosine drift dashboards and error rates
Stage 3: Scale to 25% for 72 hours if no alerts, then 100% with staggered ramping and cost/perf reporting
Rollback criteria: any drift alert triggered by Console job OR user-visible recall degradation > 2%
Notes: For Private deployments, provide a signed artifact and calibration profile; customer can run the supplied drift job on-prem
monitoring_and_alerts: Daily Drift Job: compute cohort-level cosine mean/percentiles and compare to baseline; store time-series in Console metrics
Alert rule: mean_cosine < baseline_mean - 0.01 OR recall10 < baseline_recall10 - 0.015 triggers P0 alert
Dashboard panels: per-region cosine distribution, per-model version scatter, top-k queries with largest cosine delta
Logging: attach sample inputs that caused largest delta (redact PII) for triage; link to GitHub issue template for investigation

open_questions: Should we expose 'quantization profile' as a first-class field in the model registry UI, or keep it metadata-only?
Is per-channel INT8 universally better for all embedding sizes or should we detect and fall back to per-tensor for small layers?
Do we need customer-specific calibration for enterprise customers with bespoke corpora, or is a single curated calibration set sufficient?
